chapter: The 1920s road: dance style and management
title: Who wrote the comedy and music: Bubbles' gags and Buck's Boogie
summary: Bubbles wrote the gags and song lyrics himself; Buck composed piano numbers like Buck's Boogie but did not write music down.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Who wrote your comedy?
Who wrote it?
We wrote it.
You wrote your own comedy?
Yeah, uh-huh.

How would you work it out. Where would you do it? You'd be sitting at dinner and you'd start talking about your act? Did you both get together at a particular time during the day and work together? How did your comedy evolve?

I'd get the gags together, gag him, let him answer to what I say. I'd make up the gag, I'd tell the gag to myself then I'd get to him and I'd give him the gag to do. That's how the gag would get together, you know?
So you'd sort of create it and then you'd both work on it together.
Oh, yeah. When I finish the gag here and took it to him, it's done. There ain't no more to do to it. That's it.
So they're pretty much your gags.
Yeah.
He didn't write any of them.
No, he didn't write them.
How about the music? Did he write that?
No, he didn't write no music. He wrote music, but piano numbers. He did piano numbers like "Buck's Boogie." But I didn't write nothing, I just wrote the lyrics to the songs.
You wrote the lyrics and did he write the music?
No, he don't write music. He composed music, though. He composes. What did he compose? Like the "Buck's Boogie," but that ain't no music you can use, you know?
"Buck's Boogie," how does that go?
Can't tell you
how it goes, gotta play it.
Was that ever written down? Or recorded?
Yeah.
Because I heard he was a fabulous pianist.
Yeah, he was. You can tell that from the clipping you got of him with the Varsity Show.
What have we got? I got a number here -- I've forgotten who it was with. How far are we now in that tape there?
